title: Arakhin 2
description: The first daf of Arakhin: who may pledge a valuation or an assessment and who may be valuated, and what the word “everyone” adds, in this mishna and in a string of others, from an heir’s placing of hands and substitution to sukka, appearance in the Temple and the Megilla.
topics: ⚖️ Valuation and assessment: the Torah’s fixed sum and a person’s market worth
❓ The tumtum and the hermaphrodite pledge, but are not valuated
🧒 The deaf-mute, the imbecile and the minor are valuated, but cannot pledge
➕ What “everyone” adds: the minor near adulthood, the repulsive man, the infant under a month
🐂 An heir’s offering: placing hands and substitution, Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis
🌿 Minors and mitzvot: sukka, lulav, ritual fringes, phylacteries and shofar
🏛️ Appearing in the Temple: the half-slave, the lame and the one-eyed
📜 Beit Shammai on the half-slave: “He formed it to be inhabited”

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל מַעֲרִיכִין, וְנֶעֱרָכִין, נוֹדְרִין וְנִידָּרִין — כֹּהֲנִים, לֹוִים וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים, נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים.

a2.he: טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, נוֹדְרִין וְנִידָּרִין וּמַעֲרִיכִין, אֲבָל לֹא נֶעֱרָכִין, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶעֱרָךְ אֶלָּא הַזָּכָר וַדַּאי וּנְקֵבָה וַדָּאִית.

a3.he: חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן נִידָּרִין וְנֶעֱרָכִין, אֲבָל לֹא נוֹדְרִין וְלֹא מַעֲרִיכִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם דַּעַת.

a4.he: גְּמָ׳ ״הַכֹּל מַעֲרִיכִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי מוּפְלָא סָמוּךְ לְאִישׁ.

a5.he: ״נֶעֱרָכִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי מְנוָּּול וּמוּכֵּה שְׁחִין.

a6.he: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: ״נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ כְּתִיב, כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּדָמִים — יֶשְׁנוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּדָמִים — אֵינוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין.

a9.he: ״נִידָּרִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? אִי לְאֵתוֹיֵי טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ! וְאִי לְאֵתוֹיֵי חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן — בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ!

a10.he: אִי לְאֵתוֹיֵי פָּחוֹת מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ, בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ! וְאִי לְאֵתוֹיֵי נָכְרִי, בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ! לְעוֹלָם לְאֵתוֹיֵי פָּחוֹת מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ, וְתָנֵי וַהֲדַר מְפָרֵשׁ.

a11.he: ״הַכֹּל סוֹמְכִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי יוֹרֵשׁ, וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

a12.he: ״הַכֹּל מְמִירִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי יוֹרֵשׁ, וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

a13.he: דְּתַנְיָא: יוֹרֵשׁ סוֹמֵךְ, יוֹרֵשׁ מֵימֵר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ, יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵימֵר.

a14.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ וְלֹא קׇרְבַּן אָבִיו, וְיָלֵיף תְּחִלַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ מִסּוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ — מָה סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ, אַף תְּחִלַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵימֵר.

a15.he: וְרַבָּנַן, הָמֵר יָמִיר — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַיּוֹרֵשׁ, וְיָלְפִינַן סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ מִתְּחִלַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ: מָה תְּחִלַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ — יוֹרֵשׁ מֵימֵר, אַף סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ — יוֹרֵשׁ סוֹמֵךְ.

a16.he: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ: ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ — וְלֹא קׇרְבַּן גּוֹי, ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ — וְלֹא קׇרְבַּן חֲבֵירוֹ, ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ — לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה.

a17.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה לֵית לֵיהּ, וְאִי נָמֵי אִית לֵיהּ,

b1.he: גּוֹי וַחֲבֵירוֹ מֵחַד קְרָא נָפְקִי, אִיַּיתַּרִי לְהוּ תְּרֵי: חַד ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ וְלֹא קׇרְבַּן אָבִיו, וְאִידָּךְ לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה.

b2.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָאִשָּׁה, דְּתַנְיָא: לְפִי שֶׁכׇּל הָעִנְיָן אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בִּלְשׁוֹן זָכָר, מַה סּוֹפֵינוּ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָאִשָּׁה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וְאִם הָמֵר יָמִיר״.

b3.he: וְרַבָּנַן? מִ״וְּאִם״, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה ״וְאִם״ לָא דָּרֵישׁ.

b4.he: ״הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּסוּכָּה״ — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי קָטָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְאִמּוֹ, דִּתְנַן: קָטָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְאִמּוֹ חַיָּיב בְּסוּכָּה.

b5.he: ״הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּלוּלָב״ — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לְנַעְנֵעַ, דִּתְנַן: קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לְנַעְנֵעַ חַיָּיב בְּלוּלָב.

b6.he: ״הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּצִיצִית״ — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לְהִתְעַטֵּף, דְּתַנְיָא: קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לְהִתְעַטֵּף — חַיָּיב בְּצִיצִית.

b7.he: ״הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְפִילִּין״ — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לִשְׁמוֹר תְּפִלִּין, דְּתַנְיָא: קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לִשְׁמוֹר תְּפִלִּין — אָבִיו לוֹקֵחַ לוֹ תְּפִלִּין.

b8.he: ״הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּרְאִיָּיה״ — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין.

b9.he: וּלְרָבִינָא דְּאָמַר: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין פָּטוּר מִן הָרְאִיָּיה, לְאֵיתוֹיֵי חִיגֵּר בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וְנִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי.

b10.he: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: כּוּלָּן תַּשְׁלוּמִין זֶה לָזֶה, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: כּוּלָּן תַּשְׁלוּמִין לָרִאשׁוֹן — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי?

b11.he: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי סוּמָא בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינָיו, וּדְלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא.

b12.he: דְּתַנְיָא, יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: סוּמָא בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינָיו פָּטוּר מִן הָרְאִיָּיה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יִרְאֶה״ ״יֵרָאֶה״, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁבָּא לִרְאוֹת כָּךְ בָּא לֵירָאוֹת, מַה לִּרְאוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו — אַף לֵירָאוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו.

b13.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ דְּרָבִינָא — לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּמִשְׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, כָּאן בְּמִשְׁנָה אַחֲרוֹנָה.

b14.he: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין, עוֹבֵד אֶת רַבּוֹ יוֹם אֶחָד, וְאֶת עַצְמוֹ יוֹם אֶחָד, דִּבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל.

b15.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: תִּיקַּנְתֶּם אֶת רַבּוֹ, וְאֶת עַצְמוֹ לֹא תִּיקַּנְתֶּם? לִישָּׂא שִׁפְחָה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל, בַּת חוֹרִין אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל, יִבָּטֵל? וַהֲלֹא לֹא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא לִפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ״!

b16.he: אֶלָּא, מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם, כּוֹפִין אֶת רַבּוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין, וְכוֹתֵב שְׁטָר עַל חֲצִי דָּמָיו, וְחָזְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי.

b17.he: ״הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר״ — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי קָטָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְחִינּוּךְ, דִּתְנַן: אֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַקָּטָן מִלִּתְקוֹעַ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.

b18.he: ״הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּמִקְרָא מְגִילָּה״, ״הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה״ — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי

messages.text: 2a
Masechet Arakhin begins · מסכת ערכין
Chapter 1 · הכל מעריכין · HaKol Ma’arikhin: who may pledge valuations and assessments, and who may be valuated.
Mishna
Everyone takes vows of valuation and is thereby obligated to donate to the Temple treasury the value fixed by the Torah (see Leviticus 27:3–7) for the age and sex of the person valuated.

verse.he: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃ וְאִם־נְקֵבָה הִוא וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁקֶל׃ וְאִם מִבֶּן־חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְעַד בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר עֶשְׂרִים שְׁקָלִים וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשֶׂרֶת שְׁקָלִים׃ וְאִם מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד בֶּן־חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר חֲמִשָּׁה שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף׃ וְאִם מִבֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה אִם־זָכָר וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שָׁקֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשָׂרָה שְׁקָלִים׃
verse.en: the following scale shall apply: If it is a male from twenty to sixty years of age, the equivalent is fifty shekels of silver by the sanctuary weight; if it is a female, the equivalent is thirty shekels. If the age is from five years to twenty years, the equivalent is twenty shekels for a male and ten shekels for a female. If the age is from one month to five years, the equivalent for a male is five shekels of silver, and the equivalent for a female is three shekels of silver. If the age is sixty years or over, the equivalent is fifteen shekels in the case of a male and ten shekels for a female.

notes.he: ערך כתוב בפרשה. (נדר דמי עלי ושמים אותו כעבד הנמכר בשוק):
notes.en: Mishna. Everyone takes valuations: “valuation” [erekh] is written in the Torah portion. (A vow [neder] is “my worth is incumbent upon me,” and he is assessed like a slave sold in the market.)

notes.he: אם אמר על אחד ערך פלוני עלי נותן ערך אותו פלוני כפי שניו שהערך ניתן לפי השנים הכתוב בפ' ערכין ואחר שנות הנערכים הולכים:
notes.en: Take valuations [ma’arikhin]: if one said of someone, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” he gives that so-and-so’s valuation according to his years, since the valuation is given by the years written in the portion of valuations, and one goes by the years of those who are valuated.

notes.he: בנזיר (דף ב.) ובנדרים (דף ב.) הזכיר כינויים שלא להזכיר שם שמים לבטלה כדאיתא התם ובכאן לא חשש להזכיר שלא היו מזכירין שם שמים על הערכין ערך כתוב בפרשה נדרים דמי עלי ושמין אותו כעבד הנמכר בשוק:
notes.en: Mishna. Everyone takes valuations: in Nazir (2a) and in Nedarim (2a) the mishna mentions substitute terms [kinuyim], so as not to mention the Name of Heaven in vain, as is explained there. Here the tanna was not concerned about mentioning [the terms themselves], since people did not mention the Name of Heaven with valuations. “Valuation” is written in the portion; vows are “my worth is incumbent upon me,” and he is assessed like a slave sold in the market.

notes.he: אם אמר על אחד בשוק ערך פלוני עלי (או אם אמר ערך אותו פלוני עלי) נותן לפי השנים הכתובים בפרשת שקלים ולפי שנותיו הולכים:
notes.en: Take valuations: if one said of someone in the market, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me” (or if he said, “The valuation of that so-and-so is incumbent upon me”), he gives according to the years written in the portion of shekels [Rashi reads: “the portion of valuations”], and one goes by his years.

notes.he: בין לעצמן בין לאחרים כגון ערכי עלי או ערך פלוני עלי וחייב בערכו לפי שניו:
notes.en: Everyone takes valuations: whether for themselves or for others, for example “My valuation is incumbent upon me” or “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” and he is obligated in his valuation according to his years.

messages.text: And similarly, everyone is valuated, and therefore one who vowed to donate his fixed value is obligated to pay.

notes.he: אם אמר ערכי עלי או אם אמר אחר עליו ערך פלוני עלי:
notes.en: Are valuated [ne’erakhin]: if he said, “My valuation is incumbent upon me,” or if another said of him, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me.”

notes.he: אם אמר ערכי עלי או אם אמר אחר [עליו] ערך פלוני עלי:
notes.en: Are valuated: if he said, “My valuation is incumbent upon me,” or if another said [of him], “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me.”

notes.he: שיכול אדם לומר [עליו] ערך פלוני עלי ונתפס הערך וחייב המעריך לתת ערכו:
notes.en: And are valuated: a person may say of him, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” and the valuation takes effect, and the one who made the pledge must give his valuation.

messages.text: Likewise, everyone vows to donate to the Temple treasury the assessment of a person, based on his market value to be sold as a slave, and is thereby obligated to pay; and everyone is the object of a vow if others vowed to donate his assessment.

notes.he: דמי פלוני עלי:
notes.en: Vow [nodrin]: “The worth of so-and-so is incumbent upon me.”

notes.he: דמי עלי או אם אמר אחר עליו דמי פלוני עלי:
notes.en: Are vowed [nidarin]: “My worth is incumbent upon me,” or if another said of him, “The worth of so-and-so is incumbent upon me.”

notes.he: שיכול לומר דמי עלי או דמי פלוני עלי:
notes.en: Vow: one may say, “My worth is incumbent upon me” or “The worth of so-and-so is incumbent upon me.”

notes.he: הנודר נמי (זה) שנודר ואומר דמי פלוני עלי אין לו קצבה אלא שמין אותו כעבד הנמכר בשוק ונותן דמיו:
notes.en: And are vowed: one who vows and says, “The worth of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” has no fixed sum; rather, he is assessed like a slave sold in the market, and one gives his worth.

messages.text: This includes priests, Levites and Israelites, women, and Canaanite slaves.

notes.he: ומשלמין לאחר זמן כשנתגרשה האשה או נשתחרר העבד:
notes.en: Women and slaves: and they pay later, when the woman is divorced or the slave is freed.

notes.he: משלמין לאחר זמן כשנתגרשה האשה או נשתחרר העבד כן פ"ה אי נמי כגון שנתנו להם ע"מ שאין לרב או לבעל רשות בהם ואפילו אין להם נותנין עליהם מיד כדתניא בתוספתא נשים ועבדים נודרים ונידרים אם יש להם בזמן הזה גובין מהם ואם לאו [כותבין] עליהם וגובין לאחר זמן ועבד אע"ג דגבי מצות יש לו דין אשה לפי ערך זכר הוא נערך דלא אישתמיט תנא דלימא אם היה נערך כאשה:
notes.en: Women and slaves: they pay later, when the woman is divorced or the slave is freed; so Rashi explained. Alternatively, for example where [property] was given to them on condition that the master or the husband has no rights in it. And even if they have nothing, [the debt] is placed upon them immediately, as is taught in the Tosefta: Women and slaves vow and are vowed; if they have [the means] at this time, one collects from them, and if not, one [writes a deed] against them and collects later. And a slave, although with regard to mitzvot he has the status of a woman, is valuated according to the valuation of a male, for no tanna ever let slip that he is valuated like a woman.

messages.text: A tumtum, whose sexual organs are concealed, and a hermaphrodite [androginos], vow, and are the object of a vow, and take vows of valuation, but they are not valuated.

notes.he: שהרי יש להם דמים:
notes.en: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite vow and are vowed: since they have a worth.

notes.he: את אחרים אם אמרו ערך פלוני עלי נותנין ערך אותו פלוני:
notes.en: Take valuations: of others; if they said, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” they give that so-and-so’s valuation.

notes.he: שהרי יש להם דמים ומעריכין את אחרים אם אמרו ערך פלוני עלי נותן ערך אותו פלוני אבל לא נערכין אם אמר אחד עליהם ערך פלוני עלי לא אמר כלום שזכר ונקבה אמורים בפרשה. ל"ה:
notes.en: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite vow and are vowed: since they have a worth. And they take valuations of others: if they said, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” they give that so-and-so’s valuation. But they are not valuated: if one said of them, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” he has said nothing, since male and female are what is stated in the portion. This is Rashi’s wording.

messages.text: Consequently, if one says, with regard to a tumtum: The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me to donate to the Temple treasury, he is not obligated to pay anything, as only a definite male or a definite female are valuated.

notes.he: אם אמר ערכי עלי או אם אמר אחר עליהם ערך פלוני עלי לא אמר כלום שאין להם ערך שזכר ונקבה אמורין בפרשה:
notes.en: But they are not valuated: if he said, “My valuation is incumbent upon me,” or if another said of them, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” he has said nothing, since they have no valuation, for it is male and female that are stated in the portion.

messages.caption: The Torah’s fixed valuations by age and sex (Leviticus 27:3–7). Only a male or a female is listed, so a tumtum or a hermaphrodite is not valuated.

messages.text: A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor are the object of a vow and are valuated, but neither vow to donate the assessment of a person nor take a vow of valuation, because they lack the presumed mental competence to make a commitment.

notes.he: משמע דאית ליה דמים לחרש והא דאמר פרק החובל (ב"ק פה:) חרשו נותן לו דמי כולו בחרש שאינו יכול להתרפאות אי נמי פירש ר"ת דחרש בידי שמים אית ליה דמים:
notes.en: A deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor: this implies that a deaf-mute has a worth. And as for what is said in the chapter HaḤovel (Bava Kamma 85b), “If he deafened him, he gives him his entire worth” [as though he were now worth nothing], that refers to a deafness that cannot be healed. Alternatively, Rabbeinu Tam explained that one deafened by Heaven has a worth.

notes.dh: ולא מעריכין] מפני שאין להם דעת
notes.he: דבעינן איש שיודע להפלות לשם מי הוא מעריך או נודר:
notes.en: And they do not take valuations: because they lack understanding, for we require a person who knows how to declare distinctly for whom he is pledging a valuation or making a vow.

messages.text: Gemara

What is added by the mishna’s statement: Everyone [hakol] takes vows of valuation? When a principle is stated in a mishna, it serves to include a particular case that it does not mention explicitly in its halakha. Which case is included by the broad statement here?
The mishna teaches it to add a discriminating minor on the brink of adulthood [mufla samukh le’ish], i.e., during the year before a minor reaches majority.

notes.he: בן י"ב שנה ויום אחד שהוא סמוך לאיש ואינו איש עד שיביא שתי שערות. ומופלא קרי ליה על שם שבודקין אותו אם יודע להפלות ולפרש לשם מי נדר ולשם מי הקדיש כדקתני בפ' יוצא דופן במסכת נדה (דף מה:):
notes.en: Gemara. A discriminating minor on the brink of adulthood: a boy of twelve years and one day, who is close to manhood but is not a man until he shows two hairs. He is called mufla because he is examined to see whether he knows how to make a distinct declaration [lehaflot] and specify for whose sake he vowed and for whose sake he consecrated, as is taught in the chapter Yotze Dofen in tractate Nidda (45b).

notes.he: בן י"ב שנה ויום אחד שסמוך לאיש ואינו איש עד י"ג ויום אחד ומופלא קרי ליה על שם שבודקין אותו אם יודע להפלות ולפרש לשם מי נדר לשם מי הקדיש כדקתני פרק יוצא דופן (נדה מה:):
notes.en: A discriminating minor on the brink of adulthood: a boy of twelve years and one day, who is close to manhood but is not a man until thirteen years and one day. He is called mufla because he is examined to see whether he knows how to make a distinct declaration [lehaflot] and specify for whose sake he vowed and for whose sake he consecrated, as is taught in the chapter Yotze Dofen (Nidda 45b).

notes.he: גמ' לאתויי מופלא הסמוך לאיש [היינו] תינוק בן שתים עשרה שנה ותינוקת בת י"א שנה שסמוכין למצות ונדריהן נבדקין אי הוי מופלא שיודע לשם מי הוא נודר או מעריך הוי נדר אבל קודם לזמן הזה אע"ג דהוי מופלא לא הוי נדר דחשיב כקטן ולאחר זה הזמן אע"ג דלא הוי מופלא הוי נודר:
notes.en: Gemara. To add a discriminating minor on the brink of adulthood: [that is,] a boy of twelve or a girl of eleven, who are close to [obligation in] mitzvot, and their vows are examined. If he is discriminating and knows for whose sake he vows or pledges a valuation, it is a vow. But before this age, even if he is discriminating, it is not a vow, since he is considered a minor; and after this age, even if he is not discriminating, his vow is a vow.

messages.text: What is added by the statement: And everyone is valuated?

notes.he: כלומר הכל דקאי נמי אנערכין דאכולה מתני' קאי הכל אהנערכין לאתויי מאי:
notes.en: Are valuated, to add what: that is, the word “everyone” also applies to “are valuated,” since “everyone” applies to the whole mishna. What does it add?

notes.he: כלומר הכל דקאי נמי אנערכין דאכולה מתניתין קאי הכל (לאתויי נערכין) לה"ק:
notes.en: Are valuated, to add what: that is, the word “everyone” also applies to “are valuated,” since “everyone” applies to the whole mishna; this is what it means.

messages.text: The mishna serves to add a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils, who have no market value.

notes.he: משמע דקאי נמי אעבדים דמתני' ויש להקשות דהא מיבעיא לן בפרק השולח (גיטין מב:) עבד שמכרו רבו לקנס מהו אלמא אית ליה דמים וי"ל דהכא בטריפה איירי וא"ת ההורגו יתחייב הואיל ואיתרבי בנפשות אלמא איקרי נפש דמהאי טעמא מרבינן להורג בן יום אחד פרק יוצא דופן (נדה מד:) ואף על גב דשמא נפל הוא וי"ל דהתם בתורת כהנים מוקמינן ליה בשכלו לו חדשיו וכן מוקמינן התם לר' שמעון ב"ג דאמר כל שלא שהה:
notes.en: To add a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils: this implies that it applies also to the slaves of our mishna. One may ask: we raise a dilemma in the chapter HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 42b) about a slave whom his master sold, with regard to a fine: what is the law? Evidently even [such] a slave has a worth. One may answer that here it is speaking of one who is a tereifa [with a mortal injury]. And if you say: then one who kills him should be liable, since he is included by “persons,” which shows that he is called a “person” [nefesh]; for it is for this reason that one who kills a day-old infant is included, in the chapter Yotze Dofen (Nidda 44b), even though it might be a non-viable birth — one may answer that there, in Torat Kohanim, we establish it as a case where its months were completed, and likewise we establish it there according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who says that any [infant] that did not survive [thirty days may be non-viable].

notes.he: שאין בהן דמים שאין אדם רוצה לקנותן:
notes.en: And a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils: who have no worth, since no one wants to buy them.

messages.text: This addition is necessary, as it might enter your mind to say that as it is written in the verse: “A vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:2), which juxtaposes one who is valuated to one who is the object of a vow, anyone who is included in the category of assessments, i.e., if he vows to pay his assessment he must pay it to the Temple, is also included in the category of valuations. But anyone who is not included in the category of assessments is not included in the category of valuations.

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ נְפָשֹׁת לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelite people and say to them: When anyone explicitly vows to GOD the equivalent for a human being,

notes.he: (נפשות משמע) איתקש ערכין לדמים ומנוול ומוכה שחין אינן בדמים ונודרין את אחרים אבל לא נידרין דאין שוים כלום:
notes.en: “A vow according to your valuation” is written: [the printed text adds in parentheses: “persons” implies.] Valuations are juxtaposed with worth, and a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils have no worth; they vow [the worth of] others, but they are not vowed, since they are worth nothing.

notes.he: משמע דאיתקיש ערכין לדמים מנוול ומוכה שחין אינו לדמים ונודרין את אחרים אבל לא נידרין דאין שוה כלום:
notes.en: A vow according to your valuation, persons: this implies that valuations are juxtaposed with worth. A repulsive man and one afflicted with boils have no worth; they vow [the worth of] others, but they are not vowed, since they are worth nothing.

notes.he: לאו דווקא דהא איכא דיקלא וארעא אלא כל אדם שישנו בדמים קאמר:
notes.en: Anyone who is included in assessments is included in valuations: not precisely, since there are a palm tree and land [which have a worth but no valuation]; rather, it means any person who is included in assessments.

messages.text: Since these people, a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils, are not subject to assessment, as they have no market value, perhaps they are also not subject to valuation.

Therefore, the mishna teaches us that these too are subject to valuation, as the same verse also states: “Persons [nefashot],” indicating anyone who has any amount of life [nefesh] is subject to valuation.

notes.he: משמע כל שהוא נפש: כולהו הנך דמייתי תיובתא תני להו במתניתין בהדיא:
notes.en: Persons [nefashot]: implies anyone who is a living soul [nefesh]. All of those cases that it brings as a challenge [the tumtum, the deaf-mute and the rest] are taught explicitly in the mishna.

notes.he: דאפילו נפש כל דהו כי הני דלא חשיבי נערכין:
notes.en: It teaches us: “According to your valuation, persons”: that even a person of the slightest worth, like these who are not valued, is valuated.

messages.text: What is added by the mishna’s statement: Everyone vows to donate the assessment of a person?
messages.quote: everyone vows to donate to the Temple treasury the assessment of a person

messages.text: Actually, this statement is not necessary, but it is mentioned because the continuation: And everyone is the object of a vow, was necessary.

notes.he: [כלומר] אי לאיתויי מופלא הא שמעינן ליה מהכל דנערכין אלא לא איצטריך הכל לנודר אלא משום הכל דנידרין דהכל משמע אכולה בין אנערכין בין אנודרין בין אנידרין:
notes.en: Vow, to add what: [that is,] if it is to add the discriminating minor, we already learned that from the “everyone” of “are valuated.” Rather, the “everyone” was not needed for “vow” except because of the “everyone” of “are vowed,” for “everyone” applies to all of them: to “are valuated,” to “vow” and to “are vowed.”

messages.text: What, then, is added by the clause: And everyone is the object of a vow? If one were to suggest that this serves to add a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, that cannot be correct, as they are explicitly taught in the mishna itself. And if one were to suggest that it serves to add a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, they too are explicitly taught in the mishna.

And if you say that this clause serves to add the halakha that a child who is less than a month old, who is not subject to valuation, is nevertheless subject to assessment, this too is explicitly taught in a mishna (5a). And if one were to say that it serves to add a gentile, that is also explicitly taught in a mishna (5b).

Actually, the phrase: And everyone is the object of a vow, is mentioned in the mishna in order to add a child who is less than a month old, and the mishna teaches this halakha in general terms and then explains it in detail later.

notes.he: והוא הדין נמי מצי למנקט חד מהנך אלא חד מתרתי תלת נקט. ל"א להכי נקט האי משום דפליגי רבנן ור"מ בהאי פירקא (לקמן ערכין דף ה.) המעריך פחות מבן חדש ר"מ אומר נותן דמיו אדם יודע שאין ערך לפחות מבן חדש וגמר ואמר לשם דמים וחכ"א לא אמר כלום ולהכי סתמה ברישא לאשמועי' ממשנה יתירא דאפי' לרבנן היכא דאמר דמיו עלי יש לו דמים ונותן דמיו מפי מורינו:
notes.en: He teaches and then explains: and the same is true for the others; he could have taken any one of them, but he took one of the two or three. Another version: he took this one because Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis disagree about it in this chapter (below, 5a). One who valuates a child less than a month old: Rabbi Meir says he gives its worth, since a person knows that there is no valuation for one less than a month old, and he resolved to mean its worth; and the Rabbis say he has said nothing. That is why the mishna stated it anonymously at the start, to teach us from the extra wording of the mishna that even according to the Rabbis, where he said “His worth is incumbent upon me,” the child has a worth and he gives its worth. From the mouth of our teacher.

notes.he: דנידר ואע"ג דקתני ליה בהדיא במתניתין תני והדר מפרש (בגמרא) [במתני'] דמהכל מייתי ליה ואי אמרת מאי שנא (דמהאי דקאמר) תני והדר מפרש [הכי מצי למימר בין אטומטום בין אחרש בין העובד כוכבים תני והדר מפרש] [י"ל] אין הכי נמי אלא אגב דבן חדש כתיב באורייתא קא מרבי לפחות מבן חדש אע"ג דאינו נערך ולא מעריך נידר:
notes.en: Rather, to add one less than a month old, who is vowed [i.e., his assessment may be pledged]. And although it is taught explicitly in the mishna, he teaches and then explains in the mishna, since he derives it from “everyone.” And if you say, what is different [about this case]? [An editor’s note: it seems it should read: why does it say “he teaches and then explains” only about this one, when he could have said it about the others too?] He could have said “he teaches and then explains” about the tumtum, the deaf-mute and the gentile as well. One may answer: indeed so; but since “a month old” is written in the Torah, it includes one less than a month old, who, although he is neither valuated nor takes valuations, is vowed.

messages.caption: Who may pledge a valuation or an assessment, and who may be the object of one: the mishna’s list, and what the Gemara says “everyone” adds.

messages.text: What is added by the mishna (Menaḥot 93a): Everyone who brings an offering places hands on the head of the animal?
messages.lead: § The Gemara inquires about similar general expressions that appear in other mishnayot.

notes.he: קא בעי למידרש השתא כולהו הכל לריבויא:
notes.en: Everyone places hands: it now seeks to expound every “everyone” as an inclusion.

messages.text: This clause serves to add that an heir places hands on the offering of the deceased, and the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda that an heir does not place his hands on an offering he inherited.

notes.he: אדם שהפריש אביו קרבן ולא הספיק להקריבו עד שמת:
notes.en: An heir: a person whose father set aside an offering and did not manage to sacrifice it before he died.

messages.text: What is added by the ruling of the mishna (Temura 2a): Everyone substitutes a non-sacred animal for a consecrated animal?

Here too, the mishna serves to add that an heir substitutes a non-sacred animal for his father’s consecrated animal, i.e., the non-sacred animal also becomes sanctified. And this mishna is also not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as he maintains that an heir cannot substitute a non-sacred animal for the consecrated animal he inherited.
This is the source for these two opinions of Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita:
An heir places hands on his father’s offering, and an heir can effect substitution for an offering inherited from his father.

notes.he: שאם הקדיש אביו זבח ומת קודם שסמך עליו יורש סומך על קרבן אביו:
notes.en: An heir places hands and substitutes: if his father consecrated an offering and died before placing hands on it, the heir places hands on his father’s offering.

messages.text: An heir does not place hands and an heir cannot effect substitution.

What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda? With regard to placing of hands, he expounds the term: “His offering” (Leviticus 3:2), as teaching that one places his hands only on his own offering, but not on his father’s offering.
messages.quote: An heir does not place hands

verse.he: וְסָמַךְ יָדוֹ עַל־רֹאשׁ קׇרְבָּנוֹ וּשְׁחָטוֹ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְזָרְקוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים אֶת־הַדָּם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ סָבִיב׃
verse.en: You shall lay a hand upon the head of your offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting; and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall dash the blood against all sides of the altar.

notes.he: גבי סמיכה כתיבי תלתא קרבנו גבי שלמים בויקרא ודריש ר' יהודה לחד מינייהו קרבנו ולא קרבן אביו:
notes.en: His offering: with regard to placing hands, “his offering” is written three times, concerning peace offerings in Leviticus, and Rabbi Yehuda expounds one of them: “his offering,” and not his father’s offering.

notes.he: גבי סמיכה כתיבי תלתא קרבנו בויקרא ודריש רבי יהודה לחדא מינייהו קרבנו ולא קרבן אביו לשון הקונטרס ואגב חורפיה לא עיין דהתם ליכא אלא תרי ושמא על ראשו דכתיב התם חשיב ליה כמו קרבנו א"נ משאר קרבנו דריש:
notes.en: His offering: with regard to placing hands, “his offering” is written three times in Leviticus, and Rabbi Yehuda expounds one of them: “his offering,” and not his father’s offering. That is Rashi’s wording, but in his sharpness he did not look closely, since there are only two there. Perhaps he counts “on its head,” which is written there, like “his offering.” Alternatively, he expounds it from the other instances of “his offering.”

notes.he: קרבנו וסמך ידו על קרבנו ולא על ראש קרבן אביו:
notes.en: And an heir can substitute for his father’s offering. “His offering”: “and he shall place his hand on his offering,” and not on the head of his father’s offering.

messages.text: And with regard to the ruling that an heir cannot effect substitution, Rabbi Yehuda derives the halakha of the initial stage of consecration, i.e., substitution, in which a previously non-sacred animal is consecrated, from the final stage of consecration, the act of placing hands, which is performed upon an already-consecrated animal immediately before it is slaughtered: Just as with regard to the final stage of consecration, an heir does not place hands, so too, with regard to the initial stage of consecration, an heir cannot effect substitution.

notes.he: תמורה שהיא תחלת הקדישה של בהמה זו:
notes.en: The initial stage of consecration: substitution, which is the start of this animal’s sanctity.

notes.he: סמיכה שהוא סמוך לשחיטה:
notes.en: The final stage of consecration: placing hands, which is close to the slaughter.

notes.he: תמורה שהיא תחלת הקדישה של בהמה זו סוף הקדש סמיכה שהוא סמוך לשחיטה ל"ה והאי דקרי ליה תמורה סוף הקדש בפרק הזהב (ב"מ נד:) היינו לגבי קרבנו ראשון וא"ת לילף נמי שחיטה מסמיכה ולא ישחוט יורש הא ליתא דאפילו שלוחו לא ממעט לשחיטה:
notes.en: The initial stage of consecration: substitution, which is the start of this animal’s sanctity; the final stage of consecration: placing hands, which is close to the slaughter. This is Rashi’s wording. And when substitution is called “the final stage of consecration” in the chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 54b), that is relative to the first offering. And if you say: let us derive slaughter from placing hands as well, so that an heir may not slaughter — that is not so, for even one’s agent is not excluded from slaughtering.

notes.he: דהיינו תמורה דקא משוי לה השתא להא תמורה כהקדש:
notes.en: And he derives the initial stage of consecration: that is substitution, for he now makes this substitute consecrated.

notes.he: היינו סמיכה ותכף לה שחיטה ומיכלייא הקדש וכי היכי דמסמיכה ממעט יורש הם הכי נמי מתמורה]:
notes.en: From the final stage of consecration: that is placing hands, which is immediately followed by slaughter, and the consecration comes to its end. And just as an heir is excluded from placing hands, so too from substitution.

messages.text: And from where do the Rabbis derive their opinion? The verse states: “If he shall substitute [hamer yamir] animal for animal” (Leviticus 27:10), with the doubled form of hamer yamir serving to include the heir as one capable of effecting substitution.

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

messages.text: And the Rabbis derive the final stage of consecration, i.e., the placing of hands, from the initial stage of consecration, i.e., substitution: Just as with regard to the initial stage of consecration an heir can effect substitution, so too, with regard to the final stage of consecration, an heir can place hands.

notes.he: [המר] רבויא הוא דסגי למימר אם ימיר [וילפי סוף הקדש מתחלת הקדש ילפי סמיכה מתמורה:
notes.en: Hamer yamir: [“hamer”] is an inclusion, since it would have sufficed to say “if he shall substitute” [im yamir]. And they derive the final stage of consecration from the initial stage: they derive placing hands from substitution.

messages.text: And as for the Rabbis, what do they do with this term: “His offering,” from which Rabbi Yehuda derives that an heir does not place his hands?

The Rabbis expound each mention of the term, which appears three times (Leviticus 3:2, 7, 12). One instance of “his offering” teaches that one places hands only on one’s own offering, but not on the offering of a gentile. Another instance of “his offering” teaches that one places hands only on one’s own offering, but not on the offering of another person. The third instance of “his offering” serves to include all the owners of a jointly owned offering in the requirement of placing hands, i.e., they are all required to place their hands on the offering.

notes.he: חמשה שהביאו קרבן אחד בשותפות כולן צריכין לסמוך עליו ואין אחד סומך עליו:
notes.en: All partners in an offering: five who brought one offering in partnership all must place hands on it, and one does not place hands for them all.

notes.he: וא"ת כיון דאמרינן ס"פ שתי מדות (מנחות צג:) וסמך ידו ולא יד שלוחו כ"ש לא יד חבירו וא"כ קרבנו ל"ל וי"ל] אי לאו קרבנו אמינא דידו למעוטי חבירו אתא אבל שלוחו סומך וא"ת לילף מהכא בכל התורה דאין שלוחו של אדם כמותו ואמאי יליף לה בקדושין פ"ב (דף מא:) דהוי כמותו וי"ל משום דסמיכה ויבמה ועגלה ערופה שלשה כתובין הבאין כאחד דכתיב ביבמה (דברים כה) וקראו לו הן ולא שלוחן וכן בעגלה ערופה ומדדו ולא שלוחם וא"ת לילף מינייהו דבכל דוכתא הוי שלוחו כמותו מדאיצטריך למעוטינהו וי"ל דאי לאו הני קראי דקדושין דאשמועינן דשלוחו כמותו הוה מוקמינן להני תלתא קראי דסמיכה ויבמה ועגלה ערופה לדרשא אחריתי:
notes.en: His offering, and not another’s offering: and if you say: since we say at the end of the chapter Shtei Middot (Menaḥot 93b), “And he shall place his hand” — and not the hand of his agent — all the more so not the hand of another; if so, why do I need “his offering”? One may answer: were it not for “his offering,” I would have said that “his hand” comes to exclude another, but his agent may place hands. And if you say: let us derive from here, for the whole Torah, that a person’s agent is not like himself; why then is it derived in the second chapter of Kiddushin (41b) that he is like himself? One may answer: because placing hands, the yevama and the heifer whose neck is broken are three verses that come as one. Of the yevama it is written (Deuteronomy 25), “and they shall call him” — they, and not their agent; and likewise of the heifer whose neck is broken, “and they shall measure” — and not their agent. And if you say: let us derive from them that everywhere else a person’s agent is like himself, since it was necessary to exclude these — one may answer: were it not for the verses in Kiddushin that teach us that a person’s agent is like himself, we would have used these three verses, of placing hands, the yevama and the heifer, for some other exposition.

notes.he: חמשה שהביאו קרבן בשותפות כולן צריכין לסמוך עליו ואין אחד סומך על ידי כולן:
notes.en: All partners in an offering: five who brought one offering in partnership all must place hands on it, and one does not place hands on behalf of them all.

notes.dh: קרבנו ולא קרבן עובד כוכבים כו'
notes.he: דתלתא קרבנו כתיבי בסמיכה גבי שלמים קרבנו ולא קרבן עובד כוכבים דאין קרבן עובד כוכבים טעון סמיכה קרבנו ולא קרבן חברו דאין אדם סומך על קרבן שאינו שלו קרבנו לרבות כל בעלי קרבן לסמיכה:
notes.en: His offering, and not the offering of a gentile, etc.: “his offering” is written three times concerning placing hands with peace offerings. “His offering,” and not the offering of a gentile, since a gentile’s offering does not require placing hands; “his offering,” and not the offering of another, since a person does not place hands on an offering that is not his; “his offering,” to include all the owners of the offering in placing hands.

messages.text: And how does Rabbi Yehuda respond to this claim? Rabbi Yehuda does not hold that one of the mentions serves to include all owners of a jointly owned offering in the requirement of placing hands. Rather, one of the owners places his hands on the offering on behalf of the entire group. Consequently, he is left with one spare mention of “his offering,” from which he derives that an heir does not place his hands.

notes.he: דס"ל אחד סומך לכולם ולא הוי כסומך על קרבן חבירו הואיל והוא שייך ביה:
notes.en: He does not hold this: for he holds that one places hands on behalf of them all, and it is not like placing hands on another’s offering, since he has a share in it.

notes.he: דסבירא ליה אחד סומך לכולן ולא הוי כסומך על קרבן חבירו הואיל והוא שייך ביה לשון הקונטרס. והכי משמע פרק שתי מדות (מנחות צד.) ומה תנופה שנתרבתה בשוחטין נתמעטה בחוברין סמיכה שלא נתרבתה בשוחטין אינו דין שנתמעט בחוברין ת"ל קרבנו לרבות כולן אלמא למאן דאמר דלא דריש קרבנו מתנופה יליף ליה ותנן התם אחד מניף לכולם:
notes.en: He does not hold this: for he holds that one places hands on behalf of them all, and it is not like placing hands on another’s offering, since he has a share in it. This is Rashi’s wording. And so it is implied in the chapter Shtei Middot (Menaḥot 94a): “Just as waving, which was extended to those who slaughter, was limited among partners, is it not logical that placing hands, which was not extended to those who slaughter, should be limited among partners? The verse states ‘his offering,’ to include them all.” Evidently, according to the one who does not expound “his offering,” he derives it from waving, and we learned there: one person waves for them all.

messages.text: Alternatively, one can say that Rabbi Yehuda holds that one of the mentions serves to include owners of a jointly owned offering,
2b

but he maintains that the exclusion of a gentile and the exclusion of the offering of another person from the requirement of placing hands are derived from the same one mention of “his offering” in the verse. This leaves two mentions of “his offering” for Rabbi Yehuda. One he expounds to teach that he places hands on “his offering,” but not on his father’s offering that he inherited, and the other mention remains to include all the owners of a jointly owned offering in the requirement of placing hands.

notes.he: דאין ישראל סומך על קרבן עובד כוכבים ולא על קרבן ישראל חבירו:
notes.en: A gentile and another: that an Israelite does not place hands on a gentile’s offering, nor on the offering of another Israelite.

notes.he: דהני לאו קרבנו נינהו אבל אביו איצטריך קרא דסד"א קרבנו קרינא ביה הואיל ויורש הוא:
notes.en: Are derived from one verse: since these are not “his offering.” But for his father a verse was needed, since it might have entered your mind that it is called “his offering,” since he is the heir.

notes.he: דאין ישראל סומך על קרבן עובד כוכבים ולא על קרבן חבירו (מהך) [מחד] קרא נפקי דהני לאו קרבנו נינהו אבל אביו איצטריך קרא דסד"א (דיקריב הוא לה') (ויקרא א) (ולא) משום דשקולים הם ויבואו שניהם (אלא) כי היכי שהכהן הוא מקריב קרבן שאינו שלו ס"ד שיסמוך ישראל בקרבן חבירו ובקרבן עובד כוכבים נמי ס"ד [דכהן] סומך כמו שהכהן נותן לו (כדאמר בפרק קמא דתמורה) נסכים משל ציבור כדאמר פ' קמא דתמורה (דף ב:) להכי אתא קרבנו דממעט תרווייהו דמ"מ אינו שלו:
notes.en: A gentile and another are derived from one verse: since an Israelite does not place hands on a gentile’s offering nor on another’s offering, they are derived from one verse, as these are not “his offering.” But for his father a verse was needed, since it might have entered your mind… [several words here are bracketed as doubtful in the printed text]. Just as the priest sacrifices an offering that is not his, it might have entered your mind that an Israelite places hands on another’s offering; and for a gentile’s offering too, it might have entered your mind that [a priest] places hands, just as the libations for it are given from public funds, as is said in the first chapter of Temura (2b). That is why “his offering” comes, to exclude both of them, since in any event it is not his.

notes.dh: ולר' יהודה הכי לא לאתויי אשה] לרבות כל בעלי קרבן לסמיכה
notes.he: שאם יש ב' או ג' חבירין בקרבן כלן סומכין עליו. עובד כוכבים וחברו מחד קרא נפקא דהיינו שאינו שלו:
notes.en: [An editor’s note: this should read “And according to Rabbi Yehuda it does not come for this, but to include a woman,” and it belongs above, before the comment beginning “And they derive.” — And according to Rabbi Yehuda, so; not to include a woman.] To include all the owners of an offering in placing hands: if two or three partners share an offering, they all place hands on it. A gentile and another are derived from one verse, that is, [an offering] that is not his.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Yehuda, what does he do with the use of the doubled form in this verse: “If he shall substitute [hamer yamir]”? He requires it to include a woman among those who can effect substitution.

Since the entire matter of substitution is stated in the Torah only in the masculine form, what is the reason that we ultimately come to include a woman? The verse states: “And if he shall substitute [hamer yamir],” using a doubled form.

notes.he: של תמורה:
notes.en: Since the entire matter: of substitution.

notes.he: ממה סופינו לרבות את האשה (בקרבנה) שאם המירה בקרבנה יהא מומר:
notes.en: What do we ultimately: from where do we ultimately include a woman (with her offering), so that if she substituted for her offering it would be a substitute?

notes.he: שאם המירה קרבנה יהא מומר ל"ה. לפי שכל הענין אינו מדבר אלא בלשון זכר כו' ואע"ג דכל התורה כולה נמי בלשון זכר נאמרה מ"מ אמרינן דאיתקש אשה לאיש לכל עונשין אבל בתמורה אי לאו קרא לא הויא שוה לאיש כדאיתא התם פרק קמא דתמורה (שם):
notes.en: To include a woman: so that if she substituted for her offering it is a substitute; this is Rashi’s wording. Since the entire matter speaks only in the masculine, etc.: and although the whole Torah was also stated in the masculine, nevertheless we say that a woman is juxtaposed to a man for all punishments; but with regard to substitution, were it not for the verse she would not be equal to a man, as explained there, in the first chapter of Temura.

notes.he: דכתיב לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו]:
notes.en: Speaks only in the masculine: as it is written, “He shall not exchange it nor substitute it.”

notes.he: כלומר מנין יש לנו סופינו לרבות את האשה שעושה תמורה ת"ל המר ימיר:
notes.en: What do we ultimately, to include a woman: that is, from where do we ultimately [have a source] to include a woman, so that she effects substitution? The verse states: “hamer yamir.”

messages.text: And as for the Rabbis, from where do they learn that a woman can perform substitution? They derive it from the extra “and” in the phrase: “And if he shall substitute” (Leviticus 27:10).

notes.he: מרבי אשה מוי"ו דואם]:
notes.en: And the Rabbis include a woman from the vav of “and if.”

messages.text: But Rabbi Yehuda does not expound the extra “and” in the term “and if” at all.

notes.he: כלומר וי"ו לא דריש כדאיתא בתמורה פרק קמא (שם):
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda does not expound “and if”: that is, he does not expound the letter vav, as is explained in the first chapter of Temura.

messages.text: What is added by the statement of the following baraita: Everyone is obligated in the mitzva of sukka?
This serves to add a minor who does not need his mother when he awakes in the middle of the night.
A minor who does not need his mother is obligated in the mitzva of sukka.

notes.he: מפרש במסכת סוכה (דף כח:) שניעור משנתו ואינו קורא אימא:
notes.en: Who does not need his mother: explained in tractate Sukka (28b): one who wakes from his sleep and does not call out “Mother!”

notes.he: מפרש במס' סוכה (דף כח:) כל שניעור משנתו ואינו קורא אימא. ל"ה:
notes.en: Who does not need his mother: explained in tractate Sukka (28b): anyone who wakes from his sleep and does not call out “Mother!” This is Rashi’s wording.

messages.text: What is added by the ruling of the following baraita: Everyone is obligated in the mitzva of lulav? This clause serves to add a minor who knows how to wave the lulav.
A minor who knows how to wave the lulav is obligated in the mitzva of lulav.
What is added by the statement of a baraita: Everyone is obligated in the mitzva of ritual fringes? This serves to add a minor who knows how to wrap himself in a garment.

notes.he: אם יש להם טלית ואם לא יוכל לקנות טלית אינן חייבין לא למ"ד חובת טלית ולא למ"ד חובת גברא (מנחות דף מא.) דליכא בינייהו אלא כלי קופסא ואע"ג דא"ל מלאכא לרב קטינא סדינא בקייטא וסרבלא בסיתווא ציצית מה תהא עליה כלומר וכי אתה מבקש עלילות להפטר מציצית כדמפרש התם א"ל ענשיתו (עלה) [אעשה] א"ל בעידן ריתחא ענשינן היינו דווקא באותן הימים דכל הטליתות היו בת ארבע כנפות איכא עונש לאותו שמשנה אותו להיפטר אבל בזמן הזה שרוב הטליתות פטורין אין עונש למי שאינו קונה ארבע כנפות:
notes.en: Everyone is obligated in ritual fringes: if they have a garment; but if one cannot buy a garment, they are not obligated, neither according to the one who says it is an obligation of the garment nor according to the one who says it is an obligation of the person (Menaḥot 41a), for the only difference between them is a garment kept in a chest. And as for the angel who said to Rav Ketina, “A linen sheet in summer and a cloak in winter — what will become of ritual fringes?” — that is, are you seeking pretexts to exempt yourself from ritual fringes, as explained there — and when he said to him, “Do you punish for [neglecting] a positive mitzva?” the angel answered, “At a time of wrath we punish”: that applied only in those days, when all garments had four corners, so there was punishment for one who changed his garment to exempt himself. But nowadays, when most garments are exempt, there is no punishment for one who does not buy [a garment with] four corners.

messages.text: A minor who knows how to wrap himself in a garment is obligated in the mitzva of ritual fringes.

notes.he: משום דאמר במ"ק (דף כד.) כל עטיפה שאינה כעטיפת ישמעאלים אינה עטיפה שמעטפין טליתם עד שפמם כדאיתא במדרש. ומצאתי בסילוק א' שעשה הר' יוסף ט"ע שנותן ציצית א' מלפניו ואחד מלאחריו מימין וכן לשמאל:
notes.en: Who knows how to wrap himself: because it is said in Mo’ed Katan (24a), “Any wrapping that is not like the wrapping of the Ishmaelites is not a wrapping,” for they wrap their garment up to the mustache, as explained in the Midrash. And I found in a silluk [liturgical poem] composed by Rabbi Yosef Tov Elem that one places one fringe in front and one behind on the right, and likewise on the left.

notes.he: וא"ת למ"ד חובת טלית אפי' אינו יודע יתחייב אם יש לו טלית וי"ל דמ"מ לא חייבין כלי קופסא אלא לאותן המחוייבים ויודע להתעטף והלכות גדולות פסק דקיימא לן מנחות (שם) ציצית חובת גברא הוא מדקא מברכין להתעטף בציצית דהכי דייק [בפרק ב' דשבת] [דף כה: ושם] דקיימא לן [הכי]:
notes.en: Who knows how to wrap himself: and if you say: according to the one who says it is an obligation of the garment, even if he does not know how [to wrap himself] he should be obligated if he has a garment — one may answer that in any event a garment kept in a chest is obligated only for those who are obligated and know how to wrap themselves. And Halakhot Gedolot ruled that we hold (Menaḥot, there) that ritual fringes are an obligation of the person, since we bless “to wrap ourselves in ritual fringes”; for that is how it is inferred [in the second chapter of Shabbat, 25b, and there] that we hold [so].

messages.text: What is added by the ruling of a baraita: Everyone is obligated in the mitzva of phylacteries? It serves to add a minor who knows how to preserve the sanctity of phylacteries by maintaining a state of bodily cleanliness.

notes.he: כהלכתן:
notes.en: To preserve phylacteries: as they are meant to be kept.

messages.text: With regard to a minor who knows how to preserve the sanctity of phylacteries in a state of cleanliness, his father purchases phylacteries for him.

notes.he: וגבי ציצית לא נקט לישנא דלוקח דמסתמא טלית יש לו וגבי לולב נמי יכול לצאת בלולבו של אביו אי נמי משום דתפלין דמיהן יקרים שייך בהו לקיחה:
notes.en: His father purchases phylacteries for him: with ritual fringes it does not use the expression “purchases,” since presumably he has a garment; and with lulav too he can fulfill the obligation with his father’s lulav. Alternatively, because phylacteries are expensive, the term “purchase” fits them.

messages.text: What is added by the statement of the mishna (Ḥagiga 2a): Everyone is obligated in the mitzva of appearance, i.e., the obligation to appear in the Temple and to sacrifice an offering on the three pilgrimage Festivals?

notes.he: פ"ה במס' חגיגה (דף ב.) חייבין בראיית פני עזרה אבל בירושלמי אמרי עלה הדא דאיתא בקרבן אבל בראיית פנים בעזרה אפי' טף חייבין דכתיב הקהל הנשים והטף ואינה אלא אסמכתא בעלמא דודאי דלא דומיא דהקהל הוא דממעטי' התם נשים מזכורך אלא ודאי נראה דאף בראיית פנים בקרבן (אמרינן) [מיירי] דתנן התם בסמוך הראייה שתי כסף:
notes.en: Everyone is obligated in appearance: Rashi explained in tractate Ḥagiga (2a): obligated to appear in the Temple courtyard. But in the Jerusalem Talmud they say about this: “This applies to [appearance] with an offering; but as for appearing in the courtyard, even small children are obligated, as it is written: ‘Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones.’” But that is only a mere support from the verse, for certainly [appearance] is not like the Assembly [hakhel], since there [in Ḥagiga] women are excluded by “your males.” Rather, it certainly appears that [the mishna] speaks of appearance with an offering as well, for we learned there shortly after: “The appearance offering is two silver ma’a.”

messages.text: The mishna serves to add one who is a half-slave half-freeman, e.g., a Canaanite slave who was owned jointly, and only one of his owners freed him.

notes.he: אבל עבד גמור פטור דכתיב את פני האדון ה' מי שאין לו אדון אלא הוא:
notes.en: One who is half-slave, etc.: but a full slave is exempt, as it is written, “before the Master, the Lord” (Exodus 34:23): one who has no master but Him.

notes.he: אבל עבד גמור פטור דכתיב (שמות ל״ד:כ״ג) את פני האדון ה' [מי] שאין לו אדון אלא הוא ל"ה והכי מסקינן ואע"ג דתנא בסיפא דמתני' חוץ מנשים ועבדים שאינם משוחררין ומפרשינן התם דבאינן משוחררין כולן אלא חציין צ"ל דרישא דמתניתין לפי משנה אחרונה דחזרו להם ב"ה להורות כב"ש והכי אשכחן בפ"ק דעירובין (דף ו:) ובפרק אלו טריפות (חולין מג:) לעולם הלכה כבית הלל והרוצה לעשות כב"ש עושה ומוקמינן רישא לאחר בת קול וסיפא קודם בת קול:
notes.en: One who is half-slave: but a full slave is exempt, as it is written, “before the Master, the Lord” — one who has no master but Him. This is Rashi’s wording, and so we conclude. And although the latter clause of the mishna [in Ḥagiga] teaches “except for women and slaves who are not freed,” and we explain there that it means not entirely freed, i.e., half-freed, one must say that the first clause of the mishna follows the ultimate version of the mishna, when Beit Hillel retracted to rule in accordance with Beit Shammai. We find the same in the first chapter of Eruvin (6b) and in the chapter Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 43b): “The halakha always follows Beit Hillel, and one who wishes to act in accordance with Beit Shammai may do so,” and we establish the first clause as after the Divine Voice and the latter clause as before the Divine Voice.

messages.text: One who is half-slave half-freeman is exempt from the mitzva of appearance in the Temple,
messages.lead: And according to the opinion of Ravina, who said:

notes.he: בפרק קמא דחגיגה (דף ד.) ומייתי לה מסיפא דמתניתין דהתם קתני ועבדים שאינן משוחררין:
notes.en: And according to Ravina, who said, etc.: in the first chapter of Ḥagiga (4a). He derives it from the latter clause of the mishna there, which teaches: “and slaves who are not freed.”

messages.text: that clause serves to add one who was lame on the first day of the Festival and was unable to travel, and was therefore exempt at the time, but who was healed on the second day of the Festival. This man is obligated to appear in the Temple before the end of the Festival.

notes.he: פטור מן הראייה דרגלים כתיב פרט לבעלי קבין:
notes.en: Lame: he is exempt from appearance, since “regalim” is written [“three times,” literally “three feet”], excluding those with wooden legs.

notes.he: בפרק קמא דחגיגה (דף ד.) ומייתי לה מסיפא דמתניתין דהתם קתני עבדים שאינן משוחררין וחיגר פטור מן הראיה דרגלים כתיב פרט לבעלי קבין:
notes.en: And according to Ravina, who said, etc.: in the first chapter of Ḥagiga (4a). He derives it from the latter clause of the mishna there, which teaches “slaves who are not freed.” And a lame person is exempt from appearance, since “regalim” is written, excluding those with wooden legs.

messages.text: This works out well according to the one who says that all seven days of a Festival rectify one another, i.e., the obligation to appear applies equally to all days of the Festival, not just the first. Consequently, one who was exempt on the first day is nevertheless obligated on the second day.

notes.he: בפ"ק דחגיגה (דף ט.) דהא דקתני התם חוגג והולך את כל הרגל משום דכל שבעת הימים תשלומין זה לזה שני לראשון ושלישי לשני אלמא כל חד וחד חשיב באפי נפשיה דהא אית להו תשלומין ואיכא למימר דמאן דלא חזי בראשון וחזי בשני חייב:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says: in the first chapter of Ḥagiga (9a), about what is taught there, “he celebrates throughout the Festival”: because all seven days rectify one another, the second for the first and the third for the second. Evidently each day counts on its own, since each has a make-up, and one can say that one who was not fit on the first day but was fit on the second is obligated.

notes.he: בפ' קמא דחגיגה (דף ט.) דקתני התם חוגג והולך כל הרגל משום דכל שבעת הימים תשלומין זה לזה שני לראשון ושלישי לשני אלמא כל חד וחד חשוב באפי נפשיה דהא אית ליה תשלומין ואיכא למימר למאן דלא חזי בראשון וחזי בשני חייב:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says: in the first chapter of Ḥagiga (9a), where it is taught that one celebrates throughout the Festival, because all seven days rectify one another, the second for the first and the third for the second. Evidently each day counts on its own, since each has a make-up, and one can say that one who was not fit on the first day but was fit on the second is obligated.

messages.text: But according to the one who says that the main obligation is on the first day and that all the remaining days merely rectify the first day, a person who was lame on the first day of the Festival remains exempt throughout the rest of the Festival. If so, what does the statement of the mishna in Ḥagiga 2a serve to add?

notes.he: למי שהוא ראוי ומחוייב בראשון להקריב ולא הקריב מקריב כל שבעה ומי שלא נראה בראשון שוב אינו חייב דהא כולן אינן תשלומין אלא לראשון מאי איכא למימר:
notes.en: Rectify the first: one who was fit and obligated to sacrifice on the first day and did not sacrifice may sacrifice during all seven; but one who was not [fit to] appear on the first day is no longer obligated, since they are all only a make-up for the first. What can one say?

notes.he: למי שהיה ראוי ומחוייב בראשון להקריב מקריב והולך כל שבעה ומי שלא נראה בראשון שוב אינו חייב דהא כולן אינן אלא תשלומין לראשון מאי איכא למימר:
notes.en: Rectify the first: one who was fit and obligated to sacrifice on the first day may go on sacrificing during all seven; but one who was not [fit to] appear on the first day is no longer obligated, since they are all only a make-up for the first. What can one say?

notes.dh: הניחא למ"ד כולן תשלומין זה לזה
notes.he: הא דתנן מי שלא חגג ביו"ט הראשון חוגג והולך את כל הרגל ויום טוב האחרון ואיפלוג התם תרי אמוראי דמר אמר כולן תשלומין זה לזה דכולהו בני חיובא נינהו ואע"ג דלא חזי בראשון איחזי בשני שני נמי בר חיובא הוא דאי לא עבד בשני מחייב לשלומי בשאר יומי ומר אמר כולן תשלומין דראשון הן דמאן דחזי בראשון ולא עבד משלם בשאר יומי אבל אי לא חזי בראשון אע"ג דחזי בשאר יומי לאו בר חיובא הוא:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says they all rectify one another: regarding what we learned, “One who did not celebrate on the first Festival day celebrates throughout the Festival and on the last Festival day.” Two Amoraim disagree there. One says they all rectify one another, since they are all days of obligation: although he was not fit on the first, he was fit on the second, and the second too is a day of obligation, for if he did not do so on the second he must make it up on the other days. The other says they are all a make-up for the first: one who was fit on the first and did not do so makes it up on the other days, but if he was not fit on the first, even though he was fit on the other days, he is not obligated.

messages.text: It serves to add one who is blind in one of his eyes, and teaches that he is obligated to appear in the Temple, whereas one who is entirely blind is exempt. And this ruling is not in accordance with the opinion of this tanna, Rabbi Yehuda.
As it is taught in a baraita:
One who is blind in one of his eyes is exempt from the mitzva of appearance, as it is stated: “Three times in the year all your males shall appear [yera’eh] before the Lord God” (Exodus 23:17).

verse.he: שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בַּשָּׁנָה יֵרָאֶה כׇּל־זְכוּרְךָ אֶל־פְּנֵי הָאָדֹן ׀ יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Sovereign, GOD.

messages.text: According to the way in which the verse is written, without vocalization, it can be read as yireh, meaning: Shall see, instead of yera’eh, meaning: Shall appear. This teaches that in the same manner that one comes to see, so he comes to appear, i.e., to be seen: Just as the usual way to see is with both of one’s eyes, so too, the obligation to appear applies only to one who comes with the sight of both his eyes.

notes.he: יראה כתיב וקרינא יראה כדרך שהקדוש ב"ה בא לראות אותך והוא שלם בשתי עיניו כך בא ליראות שיהא הוא נראה לך בשתי עיניך:
notes.en: Yir’eh, yera’eh: it is written yir’eh [“he shall see”], and we read yera’eh [“he shall appear”]. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to see you, and He is whole in both eyes, so one comes to appear: that He be seen by you with both your eyes.

notes.he: שנאמר יראה יראה דכתיב יראה וקרינן יראה מה הבא לראות (את) הקדוש ברוך הוא שהוא רואה לעולי רגלים הוא בשתי עיניו [ישתבח זכרו לעד ולנצח] אף אותן שבאין ליראות יחזו בב' עינים:
notes.en: As it is stated, yir’eh, yera’eh: it is written yir’eh, and we read yera’eh. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, who comes to see the pilgrims, [sees] with two eyes [may His remembrance be praised forever and ever], so too those who come to be seen should see with two eyes.

notes.he: ואיכא דאמרי מהכא ויקרא אברהם שם המקום ההוא ה' יראה אשר יאמר היום בהר ה' יראה כלומר יראה את המקום ואת הבאים שם ויראה לבאין שם:
notes.en: And some say, from here: “And Abraham called the name of that place ‘The Lord will see,’ as it is said to this day, ‘On the mount of the Lord He shall be seen’” (Genesis 22:14). That is, He sees the place and those who come there, and He is seen by those who come there.

notes.he: מה לראות כו' ואיכא דאמרי מה לראות בב' עיניו היינו [כהן] שסומא באחת מעיניו שאינו רואה את הנגעים דכתיב לכל מראה עיני הכהן אף הבא לראות בב' עיניו [למ"ה:
notes.en: Just as to see, etc.: and some say: just as seeing is with two eyes — that is, [a priest] who is blind in one of his eyes, who does not examine the marks of leprosy, as it is written, “wherever the priest’s eyes look” — so too one who comes to be seen [must come] with two eyes.

messages.text: This is one possible explanation for what is added by the general statement of the mishna in Ḥagiga 2a, according to Ravina.
And if you wish, say instead: Actually, that statement serves to include one who is half-slave and half-freeman.

And with regard to what was difficult for you according to the opinion of Ravina, that he exempts such a person from the obligation of appearance, it is not difficult: Here the ruling is in accordance with the initial version of the mishna, whereas there it is in accordance with the ultimate version of the mishna.

notes.he: קודם שהודו ב"ה היה בחזקת עבד אבל אחר שחזרו להודות הואיל ובידינו לשחררו כמשוחרר דמי שאין רשות רבו עליו ולא קרינא ביה אדון אחר:
notes.en: In the initial mishna: before Beit Hillel conceded, he had the presumptive status of a slave. But after they changed their view and conceded, since it is in our power to free him, he is considered as freed, since his master has no authority over him, and “another master” does not apply to him.

notes.he: קודם שהודו ב"ה היה בחזקת עבד אבל לאחר שחזרו להודות הואיל ובידינו לשחררו כמשוחרר דמי שאין רשות לרבו עליו ולא קרינן ביה אדון אחר ל"ה והא דמיבעיא ליה (גיטין דף מב:) במעוכב גט שחרור גבי קנס או דילמא כיון דמעוכב גט שיחרור אדון קרינא ביה יש לחלק דגבי עולה לרגל אינו אדונו שאינו יכול לעכבו מלעלות לרגל כדי לעשות מלאכתו אבל מכל מקום אדונו מיקרי:
notes.en: In the initial mishna: before Beit Hillel conceded, he had the presumptive status of a slave; but after they changed their view and conceded, since it is in our power to free him, he is considered as freed, since his master has no authority over him, and “another master” does not apply to him. This is Rashi’s wording. And as for the dilemma (Gittin 42b) about one awaiting a bill of emancipation with regard to a fine — or perhaps, since he is awaiting a bill of emancipation, he is called one who has a master — one can distinguish: with regard to going up for the Festival, he is not his master, since he cannot stop him from going up for the Festival in order to do his work; but nevertheless he is called his master.

notes.he: כבית הלל פטור מן הראיה:
notes.en: In accordance with the initial mishna: according to Beit Hillel, he is exempt from appearance.

notes.he: דחזרו בית הלל להורות כבית שמאי חייב בראיה ואע"ג דעדיין לא הוי בר חורין כיון דסופו בחירות חייב בראיה]:
notes.en: In accordance with the ultimate mishna: when Beit Hillel retracted to rule in accordance with Beit Shammai, he is obligated in appearance. And although he is not yet free, since he will ultimately be free, he is obligated in appearance.

messages.text: One who is half-slave and half-freeman serves his master one day, as he is half a slave, and works for himself one day, since he is half free. This is the statement of Beit Hillel.

You have thereby remedied the situation of his master, who fully derives benefit from all his rights to the slave, but you have not remedied his own situation. How so? He cannot marry a maidservant, as half of him is free, and a free Jew may not marry a Canaanite maidservant. He is also unable to marry a free woman, as half of him is still a slave, and a Jewish woman may not marry a Canaanite slave.

And if you say he should be idle, i.e., refrain from marrying, but isn’t it true that the world was created only for procreation, as it is stated: “For so said the Lord that created the heavens…Who formed the earth and made it, He established it. He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited” (Isaiah 45:18)?

verse.he: כִּי כֹה אָמַר־יְהֹוָה בּוֹרֵא הַשָּׁמַיִם הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים יֹצֵר הָאָרֶץ וְעֹשָׂהּ הוּא כוֹנְנָהּ לֹא־תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה וְאֵין עוֹד׃
verse.en:
For thus said GOD,
The Creator of heaven who alone is God,
Who formed the earth and made it,
Who alone established it—
Who did not create it a waste,
But formed it for habitation:
I am GOD, and there is none else.

messages.text: Rather, for the betterment of the world, i.e., so that the slave will be able to engage in procreation, the court forces his master to make him a freeman by emancipating the half that he owns. And the slave writes a bill to his master accepting responsibility to pay half his value to him over time, as currently he has no property with which to redeem himself.
And Beit Hillel ultimately retracted their opinion, to rule in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai that a half-slave must be emancipated.

The ruling of the mishna that a half-slave must appear in the Temple is in accordance with this opinion, which holds that the master must free him. Ravina’s statement that he is not obligated to appear in the Temple is in accordance with the initial mishna, according to which Beit Hillel held that the master is not forced to free the half-slave.
What is added by the statement of the baraita: Everyone is obligated to sound the shofar? This serves to add a minor who reached the age of training in mitzvot.

notes.he: פלוגתא היא בפרק בתרא דיומא (דף פב.) חד אמר כבר (שית) [שמונה] כבר (שבע) [תשע] וחד אמר כבר תשע כבר עשר שמחנכין אותו לשעות:
notes.en: Who reached the age of training: this is a dispute in the last chapter of Yoma (82a). One says: from eight, from nine [the printed text reads six and seven, corrected in brackets to eight and nine]; and one says: from nine, from ten, when one trains him [to fast] for some hours.

notes.he: פלוגתא היא בפרק ח' דיומא (דף פב.) חד אמר כבר (שית) [וחד אמר] כבר תמני וי"א כבר תשע כבר עשר שמחנכין אותו למצות ל"ה. ולא נהירא דהתם בחינוך קטן להתענות איירי אבל בשאר מצות כל אחד ואחד לפי דרכו כדאשכחן לעיל גבי לולב וסוכה ותפלין:
notes.en: Who reached the age of training: this is a dispute in the eighth chapter of Yoma (82a): one says from [six], [and one says] from eight; and some say from nine, from ten, when one trains him in mitzvot. This is Rashi’s wording. But it is not correct, for there it speaks of training a minor to fast; but in other mitzvot, each according to its own manner, as we found above with lulav, sukka and phylacteries.

notes.he: שחייב בתקיעת שופר כחינוך האמור (בערב) [בפ' יום] הכפורים (דף פב.):
notes.en: Who reached the age of training: who is obligated in sounding the shofar, like the training mentioned in [the chapter] Yom HaKippurim (82a).

messages.text: One need not prevent minors from sounding the shofar on the festival of Rosh HaShana, despite the fact that they are not obligated in mitzvot.

notes.he: בפרק ד' דר"ה (דף לג.) מקשה הספר מדקתני אין מעכבין הא לכתחילה (מעכבין) לא אמרינן להו זילו תקעו והדר תני אבל מתעסקין בהן שילמדו אפי' בשבת ומשני כאן בקטן שהגיע לחינוך כאן בקטן שלא הגיע לחינוך כלומר בקטן שהגיע לחינוך מתעסקין וא"ת פשיטא דאין מעכבין למ"ד ביבמות פרק חרש (דף קיד.) קטן אוכל נבילות אין ב"ד מצווין להפרישו וי"ל כגון שהגיע לחינוך שמירת שבת אבל לא הגיע לחינוך תקיעת שופר והוי קצת חידוש:
notes.en: One need not prevent minors from sounding: in the fourth chapter of Rosh HaShana (33a) the Gemara asks: since it teaches “one need not prevent,” it follows that we do not tell them ab initio, “Go and sound,” and then it teaches, “but one busies oneself with them so that they learn, even on Shabbat.” It answers: here it speaks of a minor who reached the age of training, there of a minor who did not; that is, with a minor who reached the age of training, one busies oneself with him. And if you say: it is obvious that one need not prevent them, according to the one who says in the chapter Ḥeresh in Yevamot (114a) that if a minor eats carcasses the court is not commanded to stop him — one may answer: for example, where he reached the age of training for keeping Shabbat but not the age of training for sounding the shofar, and so it is something of a novelty.

messages.text: With regard to the ruling of the baraita: Everyone is obligated in the mitzva of reading the Megilla, the Scroll of Esther, and the statement of the mishna (Megilla 19b): Everyone is fit to read the Megilla, these serve to add…

notes.dh: הכל חייבין במגילה והכל כשרין לקרות
notes.he: שכל המחוייב בדבר מוציא את הרבים ידי חובתן:
notes.en: Everyone is obligated in the Megilla, and everyone is fit to read it: for anyone who is obligated in a matter can discharge the obligation of the public.

messages.text: The answer comes on 3a: they add women, in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who says that women are obligated in reading the Megilla, as they too were participants in that miracle.
